_about: What the coach says during each crisis (game/training/crises.gd). Every line is recorded by tools/make_voices.py.

brief_easy.text: Arre, the lights! Don't worry, the generator kicks in within a minute. Usually. Tell me what you need, Doctor.

brief_hard.text: Lights gone, generator coughing like a Pune rickshaw. The card's on the trolley, Doctor. Read it before you do anything brave.

brief_extreme.text: Everything's dead, and the generator's diesel was 'arranged' by purchase. No hints from me today, Doctor. Your call.

s1_right_general.text: Good, the bag's going and Dr. Khan is counting breaths. Now we need light, na.

s1_wrong_general.text: Doctor, the ventilator's dead! Nobody was breathing for the patient! Dr. Khan grabbed the bag. Now light, quickly.

s1_right_spinal.text: Haan, good. Calm voice, still patient. Awake people in the dark imagine the worst. Now, light.

s1_wrong_spinal.text: The patient's awake, Doctor, and now panicking with an open wound. Dr. Khan is talking them down. Light, now.

s1_hint.text: First ask yourself who is breathing for the patient right now. Read the anaesthetic line on the card.

s2_right.text: Light! Not pretty, but light. Keep it steady on the wound, everybody.

s2_wrong_kit.text: The kit was checked on Monday, Doctor. My handwriting is on it. The headlamp was sitting right there, charged and insulted.

s2_wrong_flat.text: The headlamp is decorating somebody's balcony for Diwali, Doctor. It's on the card. Phones out, everyone.

s2_hint.text: What does the card say about the emergency kit? Use what's actually in the room, not what's supposed to be.

s3_right_keyhole.text: Hands still. Nobody moves a thing inside till the camera's back. Good.

s3_wrong_keyhole.text: Doctor, those instruments are inside a belly nobody can see. Moving them blind is how livers get personal. Hold still.

s3_right_bleeding.text: Pressure, and patience. The bleeding's slowing. My heart is not, but the bleeding is.

s3_wrong_bleeding.text: Clamping in the dark catches whatever's nearby, Doctor. And the diathermy needs power. Press. Just press.

s3_right_closing.text: Good. We stop, and count again with light. Swabs love dark corners.

s3_wrong_closing.text: Doctor, that count was from before the dark. Things fall when people panic. We count again, full stop.

s3_hint.text: Read what was happening on the card: keyhole, bleeding, or closing. Each one wants something different.

s4_right.text: Correct. The patient's numbers first. The surgeon's comfort can wait in the queue like everyone else.

s4_wrong_ups.text: Ten minutes of power, Doctor, and you spent it on the surgeon? The monitor and the anaesthetic machine keep the patient alive.

s4_wrong_dead.text: No monitor means you become the monitor, Doctor. Pulse, cuff, every three minutes, out loud.

s4_hint.text: Check the card: is the UPS alive or dead? Then ask what keeps the patient safe, not what finishes the job.

s5_right.text: Lights back, settings checked. Now we can thank the generator. Quietly.

s5_wrong.text: Arre, the lights came back, not the settings! Machines restart on their own ideas, Doctor. Check first.

s5_hint.text: The power's back. What did the machines switch on to, and is it what the patient needs?

end_all.text: Patient stable, wound clean, everyone still employed. I'm writing to the generator company. Strongly.

end_some.text: Patient's okay. Some of that was luck, Doctor, and luck doesn't come with a maintenance contract.

end_none.text: Patient survived, thanks to Dr. Khan and God, in that order. We'll practise this in daylight, na?

brief_easy.text: Two Ramesh Kumars, Doctor. Same age, same ward, one gallbladder between them. Check properly, please.

brief_hard.text: Two Ramesh Kumars, and the night staff banded them in a hurry. Somebody's band may be lying. Look closely.

brief_extreme.text: Two Ramesh Kumars, a hurried night shift, and theatre shouting for the nine o'clock. No hints today, Doctor. Read every digit.

s1_right.text: Exactly. His own name and birthday, and the band against the slip. Not 'You're Ramesh, na?'.

s1_wrong.text: Doctor, every hungry man says yes to 'You're Ramesh, na?'. Two identifiers: his own mouth, and his band.

s1_hint.text: Which checks can't be fooled by a polite patient or a lazy whiteboard? Pick only those.

s2_right_clean.text: Correct. His birthday, his band and the slip all agree. The other Ramesh gets breakfast and an apology.

s2_right_misprint.text: Well caught. His birthday matches, but his band's number is swapped. We re-band him, then theatre.

s2_right_swapped.text: Very good. Their birthdays match each other's bands. Swapped! Nobody moves till they're re-banded.

s2_wrong.text: Doctor, read the digits again. What he said, what his band says, what the slip says. All three, or nobody goes.

s2_hint.text: Match each man's spoken birthday to his own band, then the band to the slip. Every digit, not just the name.

s3_right.text: Right. Clear fluids two hours, milk and food six. You've just saved me a fight with anaesthesia.

s3_wrong.text: Doctor, clear fluids are two hours. Milk, chai and food are six. Count from what he had, not from what he wishes he hadn't.

s3_hint.text: Is what he had a clear fluid or food? Clear is two hours. Milk, chai, biscuits and food are six.

end_all.text: Right man, right band, right time. Theatre's happy. The other Ramesh is happier. He's eating poha.

end_some.text: We got there, Doctor. Slowly. Theatre sends their love, and their schedule.

end_none.text: Doctor, if I hadn't checked again, the wrong Ramesh would be losing a perfectly good gallbladder. Please.

brief_easy.text: Twenty relatives, one corridor, and the security guard is 'on tea'. They want a doctor. That's you.

brief_hard.text: They're angry, Doctor, and someone's filming. Read the card. See what they're actually angry about.

brief_extreme.text: It's getting ugly out there. Security is 'coming'. Keep your voice low, and no hints from me today.

s1_right.text: Good. The next of kin first. The volume can wait outside.

s1_wrong.text: Doctor, the loudest person is never the one who has the right to know. Find the next of kin.

s1_hint.text: Who actually has the right to hear this first? Not the one with the biggest voice.

s2_right.text: Good. Chairs, a closed door, and I stay. Nobody gets bad news standing up.

s2_wrong.text: Arre, Doctor, not like that! Bad news is given sitting down, in a private room, with a nurse.

s2_hint.text: Where would you want to hear the worst news of your life? Not standing in a corridor.

s3_right.text: That's it. You said sorry for exactly what was hurting them. Listen to how quiet it's gone.

s3_wrong.text: Doctor, listen to what they're shouting about. Answer that, in plain words, first.

s3_hint.text: The card says what they keep repeating. Say sorry for that, plainly, before anything else.

s4_right.text: Good. Calm, out, together. Security's here now. Nobody was a hero, and everybody's fine.

s4_wrong.text: Doctor! When something becomes a weapon, the talking is over. Out, calmly, and call one one two.

s4_hint.text: Is this still a conversation, or has it become something else? Safety first, explanations later.

s5_right_accident.text: Gently and correctly. A road accident is a medico-legal case. Kindness is explaining that, not skipping it.

s5_wrong_accident.text: Doctor, a death after an accident must be reported. The police and the post-mortem are the law, not our choice.

s5_right_natural.text: Correct. A known cause gets a certificate, not a post-mortem. The corporator will find someone else to shout at.

s5_wrong_natural.text: Doctor, a natural death with a known cause needs a death certificate. Not a post-mortem to calm a politician.

s5_hint.text: Was this an accident, or an illness with a known cause? That decides what the law asks for.

end_all.text: They're still crying, but they're not shouting. That's the best this room ever gets, Doctor.

end_some.text: It calmed down. Some of that was you, some was the chai I sent in. Let's not ask which.

end_none.text: Doctor, that went badly, and the video's already on three WhatsApp groups. We'll talk about this.

brief_easy.text: Five family members, all very keen, all very sure they're perfect donors. Check them, Doctor.

brief_hard.text: Six donors, and every one of them says 'I'm totally healthy'. They also said the uncle doesn't drink.

brief_extreme.text: Seven donors, three units needed, and a family that lies with love. No hints today, Doctor.

s1_right.text: Every unit compatible and safe. The blood bank is impressed, and they're never impressed.

s1_wrong.text: Doctor, not everyone on that list can give. Check the group, the limits, and the small print: drinks, tattoos, tablets.

s1_hint.text: First the group: can it go into this patient? Then age, weight, haemoglobin, and what they've had recently.

s2_right.text: Two of us, at the bed, against the band. Boring and correct, the best kind of correct.

s2_wrong.text: Doctor, a name on the bag isn't enough. Two people check it at the bed, against the band. Every time.

s2_hint.text: Most transfusion disasters are the wrong bag in the right patient. How do we stop that?

end_all.text: Blood's running, the patient's pinking up, and the uncle has been told, kindly, to stop drinking at weddings.

end_some.text: The patient's getting blood. One donor's going home very offended. He'll live.

end_none.text: Doctor, the blood bank sent half of them back. Please read the donor rules. I'll laminate them for you.

brief_easy.text: The TPA has returned the form. Two mistakes, they say. I say, find them before they find more.

brief_hard.text: The insurer's desk has a new officer. Young, keen, reads everything. Terrible. Check every field.

brief_extreme.text: This one reads forms with a magnifying glass, Doctor, and he dislikes hospitals. No hints. I am not a doctor.

s1_right.text: Every mismatch found. The TPA will have to invent a new reason to reject us. They will, but still.

s1_wrong.text: Doctor, the insurer will find what you missed. They're paid to. Check the form against the documents, letter by letter.

s1_hint.text: Lay every line next to the Aadhaar, the policy card, the doctor's note and the costing sheet. Letter by letter.

s2_right.text: Correct. Waiting periods: the first thirty days, then the specific ones. The family hears it from us, today.

s2_wrong.text: Doctor, read the policy date. First thirty days, nothing except accidents. Some illnesses wait two years. And no fake accidents.

s2_hint.text: How long has the policy been running, and is this an emergency or a planned operation like a hernia?

s3_right.text: Patient first, paperwork second. The accounts department will faint, but they faint every month.

s3_wrong.text: Doctor, an appendix doesn't wait for approval. Operate. Approval or the bill follows. My department will cope. Somehow.

s3_right_hernia.text: The truth on the form, and help with the cost. Even I can't find a flaw in that, and I try.

s3_wrong_hernia.text: Doctor, the insurer checks. 'Emergency hernia, two years old' gets the hospital blacklisted. Write what it is.

s3_hint.text: What does the patient need right now, and what will the form honestly say?

end_all.text: Claim clean, family informed, nobody committed fraud. I may put you on the billing committee. That's a threat.

end_some.text: The claim went in. It'll come back once, as all claims do. Next time, fewer surprises, please.

end_none.text: Doctor, the claim's rejected, the family is upset, and I have a headache. Please learn the policy rules.

brief_easy.text: Snakebite, Doctor, two hours on a tempo from the village. Read the signs. The snake isn't here to ask.

brief_hard.text: Snakebite, and the village is very sure what snake it was. They're usually wrong. The signs aren't.

brief_extreme.text: Snakebite, middle of the night, no senior answering. The antivenom fridge is open. No hints, Doctor. Go.

s1_right.text: Right. The signs and the clotting test together. Now, the antivenom.

s1_wrong.text: Doctor, read it again. Drooping and trouble swallowing is the nerves. Bleeding, and blood that won't clot, is the blood.

s1_hint.text: Look at the eyelids and the swallowing, then the gums, the urine and the twenty-minute clotting test.

s2_right.text: Ten vials, slowly, adrenaline drawn up. Snakes don't do half measures, so neither do we.

s2_right_none.text: Correct. No signs of venom, no antivenom yet. We watch, and repeat the clotting test every six hours.

s2_wrong.text: Doctor, with venom signs it's ten vials, children included. With no signs, none yet. Half doses help nobody.

s2_hint.text: Are there any signs of venom at all? If yes, the dose doesn't shrink for anyone.

s3_right.text: Good. First aid fixed without making it worse. The village will be told, nicely, about ropes and razors.

s3_wrong.text: Doctor, that makes it worse. Ropes are loosened slowly after the antivenom, cuts are cleaned, splints stay.

s3_hint.text: What did the village actually do, and how do we undo it without flooding the body with venom?

s4_right.text: Right call. You're thinking about the hours after, not just the minutes. That's the job.

s4_wrong.text: Doctor, the next six hours matter as much as the first. Breathing first, repeat doses, and no early discharge.

s4_hint.text: What is the venom doing now: still bleeding, weaker breathing, or nothing at all?

end_all.text: Stable, and the family has stopped arguing about which snake it was. Mostly.

end_some.text: They'll be okay. Some of that was you, Doctor, and some of that was a very forgiving snake.

end_none.text: Doctor, the registrar had to come in at four in the morning. He is not happy. Let's revise snakebite, na?

brief_easy.text: Five families, two units of platelets, and every one of them has a cousin who's a doctor on WhatsApp. Decide.

brief_hard.text: Six patients, two units, and on most of these sheets the platelet count is the least interesting number.

brief_extreme.text: Seven patients, two units, and two of them are in trouble their families can't see. No hints today, Doctor.

s1_right.text: Good. Platelets to the two who need them, fluids for the ones in danger, and home for the rest.

s1_wrong.text: No. The count isn't everything. Shock needs fluids, warning signs need the ward, and platelets are for the very low or the bleeding.

s1_hint.text: Look for shock first: the pulse pressure, cold hands. Then bleeding. Then the count. Then warning signs.

s2_right.text: Paracetamol only, fluids, and the truth about papaya. You'll be very popular. Not.

s2_wrong.text: Ibuprofen thins the blood when the platelets are already low. Paracetamol only. And papaya isn't a drip.

s2_hint.text: Which painkillers make bleeding worse? And can a juice replace the fluids in a drip?

end_all.text: Two units, the two right patients, and nobody in shock left on the ward. That's dengue season done properly.

end_some.text: Most of them are where they should be. Most. In dengue season, most isn't quite enough.

end_none.text: Doctor, someone in shock waited on the ward and the platelets went to the wrong arm. Read the warning signs again.

brief_easy.text: The inspectors are parking, Doctor. Thirty minutes. Safety first. The damp patch can stay damp.

brief_hard.text: Thirty minutes, ten jobs, and the inspectors always open the sluice room. Always.

brief_extreme.text: Twenty-five minutes, twelve jobs, and the lead inspector is the one who shut a hospital in Satara. No hints.

s1_right.text: Everything that keeps patients safe, done honestly, and on time. I could hug you, but they're watching.

s1_wrong.text: Doctor, the crash cart, the oxygen and the drugs register come before pretty beds. And we never hide anything.

s1_hint.text: What hurts a patient if it's wrong? Do those first. And the crash cart needs its key before anything else.

s2_right.text: Honest, with the paperwork. The inspector actually smiled. Nineteen years here, I've never seen that.

s2_wrong.text: Doctor, expired vials happen everywhere. Lying about them closes wards. Show the log.

s2_hint.text: Expired drugs happen in every hospital. What happens to the ones that lie about it?

over_budget.text: That won't fit in the time we have, Doctor. Something else has to go first.

end_all.text: Passed, with a remark that says 'well maintained'. I'm framing it. Next to my retirement countdown.

end_some.text: Passed, with three remarks. Mr. Malhotra wants a meeting. Mr. Malhotra always wants a meeting.

end_none.text: We failed, Doctor. The ward's on notice. And somebody hid a BP machine. Somebody.

brief_easy.text: Sixty seconds, Doctor. Casualty doesn't wait for you to finish your chai. Read the card, then decide.

brief_hard.text: One minute on the clock, and the facts are hiding in the small print. Like every patient's history, na.

brief_extreme.text: Sixty seconds, no hints, and a patient who did not read the textbook. Go.

wrong.text: No. Read the card again, and faster.

hint.text: Every answer is on the card. One number decides it. Find the number.

end_all.text: Every answer right, inside the minute. Don't let it go to your head. Tomorrow's case is already waiting.

end_some.text: Some right, some not. In casualty that's called a normal Tuesday. Same time tomorrow.

end_none.text: Not one. I'm not angry, I'm just disappointed. Read the explanations, and come back tomorrow.
